mainTopic: Consecrating part of an animal, 'for the מזבח' pledges, and ערך vows on a baby or a utensil
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about someone who says 'the leg of this animal is an עולה.' רבי מאיר says only the leg is holy, so the animal is sold to be brought as an עולה, and only the money for the leg is holy. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say the whole animal becomes an עולה. The גמרא uses this to challenge רבא. Even רבי מאיר agrees that consecrating a vital part makes the whole animal holy. רבא answers in steps, distinguishing קדושת הגוף from קדושת דמים, a whole animal from one limb, and an unblemished animal from a blemished one. Three questions about pledges 'for the מזבח' follow, from רבה, רבא and רב אשי, and all end in תיקו. Then a new משנה teaches that a baby under one month can be pledged by his value but has no ערך. The גמרא explains that רבי מאיר and the רבנן argue over whether a person ever speaks for nothing. It also shows that רב's ruling about the ערך of a utensil follows only רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Consecrating just the leg: only the leg becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether saying 'the leg of this animal is an עולה' makes the whole animal an עולה. It answers no, based on the word 'ממנו' (of it) in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'The leg of this animal is an עולה,' you might think the whole animal becomes an עולה. The פסוק says 'anything of it that one gives to ה׳ shall be holy.' Only the part 'of it' is holy, not the whole animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possibility, that the whole animal becomes holy, and rejects it from a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ממנו' means 'of it,' which is part of the animal. So the פסוק teaches that holiness goes only to the part the person named. Here the leg becomes holy and the rest of the animal does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
'One might think': it raises a possibility that will be rejected
'The פסוק teaches': it introduces the proof from a פסוק
'Of it': only part of the animal

phrases.english: "The leg of this animal is a burnt offering"
one might think the whole animal will be a burnt offering?
Therefore the verse states:

phrases.aramaic: ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַה׳ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״ —
phrases.english: "Anything of it that one gives to the Lord shall be sacred"
the part "of it" is sacred, but not all of it is sacred.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל תְּהֵא כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'the leg of this animal is an עולה' makes only the leg holy, not the whole animal (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: The holy leg cannot lose its holiness
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the leg can go back to being non-holy. The word 'יהיה' teaches that it stays holy as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the leg could become non-holy. The פסוק says 'it shall be,' which means it stays in its holy state.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a second possibility, that the leg could lose its holiness, and rejects it from the word 'יהיה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that is only partly holy cannot be offered as it is. So you might have thought the leg's holiness simply drops away. The word 'יהיה' (it shall be) teaches that the holiness stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-holy, ordinary status
'It shall be': read here as 'it stays as it is'
In its existing state

phrases.english: One might think it can go out to non-sacred status?
Therefore the verse states: "Shall be"
meaning it shall remain as it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 1. Once only the leg is holy, the ברייתא asks whether that holiness can be removed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leg's holiness stays and cannot be removed.

steps.title: The practical solution: sell the animal for an עולה
steps.stepSummary: Two rules seem to clash: only the leg is holy, and that holiness cannot be removed. The ברייתא explains what to do. Sell the animal to someone who needs an עולה. All the money is non-holy except the value of the leg. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: So how does this work? The animal is sold to someone who will bring it as an עולה. The money from the sale is non-holy, except the money for that one limb. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא combines the two rules from steps 1 and 2 into a practical plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer brings the whole animal as an עולה, so the holy leg ends up on the מזבח as it should. The seller keeps the money for the non-holy parts. Only the money for the leg must be treated as holy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So how does this work?': it asks how two rules fit together
For the needs of עולה offerings
Money, the price received
Limb, a body part

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: only the named limb is holy. The animal is sold for an עולה, and only the money for that limb is holy.

phrases.english: How is this so?
It should be sold for the needs of burnt offerings,
and its payment is non-sacred,
except for the payment for that limb of it,
the statement of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings together the rules of steps 1 and 2 into one practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The animal is sold to be brought as an עולה. Its money is non-holy except the value of the holy limb.

steps.title: The other view: the whole animal becomes an עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון hold that consecrating the leg makes the whole animal an עולה. They learn this from the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: How do we know that if someone says 'the leg of this animal is an עולה,' the whole animal becomes an עולה? The פסוק says 'anything of it that one gives to ה׳ shall be holy.' This comes to include the whole animal.
steps.whatsHappening: Three תנאים disagree with רבי מאיר. They say the holiness spreads to the whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same פסוק but read it in opposite ways. רבי מאיר focuses on 'ממנו' to limit the holiness to the leg. These תנאים read the פסוק as including the whole animal.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do we know?': it asks for a source
To include, to widen the rule

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions quote the exact same פסוק. Watch which word each side focuses on.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
From where is it derived that one who says "The leg of this animal is a burnt offering"
that all of it becomes a burnt offering?
The verse states:

phrases.aramaic: ״כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַה׳ יִהְיֶה קֹּדֶשׁ״,
phrases.english: "All that any man gives of it to the Lord shall be holy"
to include all of it.
phrases.notes: They read 'יהיה' (it shall be) as spreading the holiness to the whole animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים: מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר's ruling in steps 1–3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Consecrating the leg makes the whole animal an עולה.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר agrees about a vital body part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבי מאיר's view. He says only the named part is holy when it is a part the animal can live without. If the part is one the animal cannot live without, the whole animal becomes holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who says the whole animal is not an עולה, that is only when he consecrated a part the animal's life does not depend on. But if he consecrated a part the animal's life depends on, the whole animal becomes holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses a limit that everyone agrees to as a challenge against רבא's earlier reading of the ברייתא about consecrating an animal's head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leg is not vital, so רבי מאיר says its holiness stays in the leg. A vital part, such as the head, is different, and the holiness spreads to the whole animal. רבא had read the ברייתא where only the head is holy as consecration for the מזבח, but by this rule the whole animal should then be holy.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The one who says': it refers to a sage's opinion
'These words apply': it limits a rule to a certain case
He consecrated
A body part the animal's life depends on

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree: consecrating a vital body part makes the whole animal holy. They only disagree about a part like a leg.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because even רבי מאיר accepts this rule, רבא cannot escape the challenge by siding with one תנא. He has to give a new answer in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה,
phrases.english: And even according to the one who says not all of it is a burnt offering,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, from step 3.

phrases.english: that applies only where he consecrated
an item that its life does not depend on,
but an item that its life depends on —
the entire animal is consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה, הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי מאיר's view from step 3 and sets up a broader challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that consecrating a vital body part makes the whole animal holy.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's earlier reading that the ברייתא in which consecrating the head does not make the whole animal holy speaks of consecration for the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even רבי מאיר agrees that consecrating a vital part makes the whole animal holy. So if that ברייתא speaks of consecration for the מזבח, the whole animal should be holy, not just the head.

steps.title: רבא's new answer: holiness on the body versus holiness on the value
steps.stepSummary: רבא settles the clash between the two ברייתות. One speaks of קדושת הגוף, where the whole animal becomes holy. The other speaks of קדושת דמים, where only the head's value is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there is no difficulty. This source is talking about holiness on the body itself. That source is talking about holiness on the value only.
steps.whatsHappening: Two ברייתות seem to disagree about someone who consecrates an animal's head. In one, the whole animal becomes holy. In the other, only the head does. רבא drops an earlier answer (that is what אלא means) and gives a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person consecrates the head so it can be offered on the מזבח (קדושת הגוף), the whole animal becomes holy. If he only consecrates its value, so the money can buy קרבנות (קדושת דמים), only the head is holy. The two sources describe two different kinds of consecration, so they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that an earlier answer is being dropped and a new one is coming.
It is not difficult. This is the standard way of opening an answer to a contradiction.
Holiness on the body itself. The animal or item itself is meant to be offered.
Holiness on the value only. The item is holy for its money worth, which is used to buy קרבנות.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of holiness. In קדושת הגוף, the animal itself goes on the מזבח. In קדושת דמים, only its money value is holy.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this one is about holiness of the body itself,
that one is about holiness of the value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces an earlier answer to the contradiction about consecrating a part the animal cannot live without.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source describes a different kind of consecration.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly disagree about whether consecrating the head makes the whole animal holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Consecrating the head with קדושת הגוף makes the whole animal holy. Consecrating it with קדושת דמים makes only the head holy.

steps.title: אביי: you yourself said value-holiness becomes body-holiness
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא with his own earlier ruling. Consecrating a male animal for its value gives it קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it you, Master, who said that if someone consecrates a male animal for its value, it becomes holy with holiness of the body itself?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's answer by quoting a ruling that רבא himself gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had ruled that a male animal consecrated only for its value still gets קדושת הגוף. If so, consecrating 'for value' can still make the animal itself holy. That seems to erase the line רבא just drew between the two ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: Master. A respectful way of saying 'you' to a teacher or colleague.
A male animal
For its value, meaning for its money worth

phrases.english: But isn't it the Master who said:
phrases.notes: אביי is speaking to רבא and politely calling him 'Master.'

phrases.english: one who consecrates a male animal for its value,
it is holy with holiness of the body itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's distinction in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that consecrating for value means only the head is holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא himself ruled that consecrating a male for its value creates קדושת הגוף. So 'for value' cannot be the reason the animal stays without body-holiness.

steps.title: רבא: the whole animal versus one limb
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that his ruling covers only someone who consecrated the whole animal for its value. Someone who consecrated a single limb for its value does not create קדושת הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. That ruling is where he consecrated the whole animal. This case is where he consecrated only one limb.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends himself by narrowing his earlier ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the whole male animal is consecrated for its value, it becomes holy in its body. When only one limb is consecrated for its value, the animal does not get קדושת הגוף. So the ברייתא in which only the head is holy fits a case of one limb consecrated for value.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the whole animal
A limb or body part

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this is where he consecrated all of it,
phrases.notes: 'This' is רבא's ruling about the male animal from step 7.

phrases.english: that is where he consecrated one limb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 7 by limiting רבא's earlier ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the whole animal versus a single limb.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any consecration for value, even of one limb, gives the animal קדושת הגוף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only consecrating the whole animal for its value gives קדושת הגוף. Consecrating one limb for its value does not.

steps.title: אביי: the one-limb case was an open question for רבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that consecrating a single limb for its value was an unsolved question asked by רבה. So רבא cannot treat it as settled.
steps.simpleTranslation: About one limb too, we had an open question. For רבה asked: if someone consecrated a limb for its value, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's answer. The very case רבא treats as clear was an unanswered question for רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer depends on knowing that consecrating one limb for its value does not make the whole animal holy. But רבה asked this exact question and left it open. If the ברייתא really taught it, רבה could have answered his question from there. That suggests the ברייתא is not speaking about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
A question or dilemma that was raised, often left unsolved
What is the law?

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא tests a proposed answer. If the answer would solve a question that a great sage left open, the answer itself becomes doubtful.

phrases.english: One limb also,
was an open question for us,
phrases.notes: The point is left unsaid: if the ברייתא settled this, why was it still a question?

phrases.english: for רבה asked:
if one consecrated a limb for its value, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אֵבֶר נָמֵי אִיבְּעוֹיֵי אִיבַּעְיָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the ברייתא shows consecrating one limb for value does not create קדושת הגוף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה left this exact case as an open question. If the ברייתא clearly taught the answer, there would have been no question, so רבא's reading of the ברייתא seems wrong.

steps.title: The open question was only about an unblemished animal
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבה's unsolved question was about a תם. Our ברייתא is about a בעל מום, like a donkey, so only the value is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we asked the question, it was about an unblemished animal. Here the case is a blemished animal, just like the donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's challenge from Step 9. He shows that the ברייתא is not deciding רבה's open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's doubt was about a תם, an animal that can go on the מזבח. There, the holiness might spread to the whole animal. A בעל מום can never be offered, just like a donkey, so it cannot get קדושת הגוף, and only the value of the named limb is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: An unblemished animal, fit to be an offering
A blemished animal, which cannot be offered on the מזבח
Similar to, like
Donkey, an animal that can never be an offering

phrases.english: When we raised the question, it was about an unblemished animal;
here it is about a blemished animal,
similar to the donkey.
phrases.notes: A donkey can never go on the altar, so the blemished animal here is in the same position.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי איבעי לן בתם הכא בבעל מום
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection in Step 9 by narrowing what רבה's question was about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: unblemished versus blemished
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's unsolved question covers every case of one limb consecrated for its value, so the ברייתא could not decide it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The open question was only about a תם. A בעל מום like the donkey clearly does not get קדושת הגוף.

steps.title: Even an unfit-for-the-altar case was left open
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבה also asked about something unfit for the altar: a person pledging ״the value of my head״.
steps.simpleTranslation: We asked about a blemished case too. For רבה asked: someone who says 'The value of my head for the altar', what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's answer. He points to a case that can never be an offering, and רבה still left it as an open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can never be brought on the מזבח, so he is like a בעל מום. Yet רבה did not treat that case as obvious. So רבא's split between a תם and a בעל מום does not seem to explain why רבה's question was open.

keyTerms.meaning: A question that was asked as a real doubt
The value of my head
For the altar, meaning to buy offerings

phrases.english: A blemished case too
we also raised as a question,
for Rabba asked:
'The value of my head for the altar' — what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בעל מום נמי איבעויי איבעיא לן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבה's open question was only about a תם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה also asked about a person, who is never fit for the מזבח. So a case unfit for the altar was not obvious to him either.

steps.title: That question came before we knew this ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבה asked about ״the value of my head״ before he heard this ברייתא. Now the ברייתא settles it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we asked that question, it was before we heard this ברייתא. Now that we have heard it, we no longer ask it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי. He says רבה's question about a person is now settled by this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not deny that רבה asked about a case unfit for the altar. He says that question was asked before this ברייתא was known. Now the ברייתא teaches that in such a case only the named part's value is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: A taught source; here, the ברייתא under discussion
Before
Now

steps.confusionAlert: Here מתניתא does not mean our משנה. It means the ברייתא the גמרא has been discussing.

phrases.english: When we raised that question,
it was before we heard this baraita;
now that we have heard this baraita —
we no longer ask it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי אבעיא לן מקמי דאשמעה להא מתניתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: the question came before the source was known
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's question about a person is still open, so the ברייתא cannot be settling such cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא resolves it: in a case unfit for the altar, only the named part's value is holy.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's position stands. A limb consecrated for its value in an animal unfit for the altar makes only that value holy, and the ברייתא settles even רבה's question about a person.

steps.title: רבה's question in full
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבה's question. Does ״the value of my head for the altar״ follow the importance of the head, and so mean the whole value, or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the matter itself. רבה asked: someone who says 'The value of my head for the altar', what is the law? Is it judged by its importance, or is it not judged by its importance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at רבה's question on its own and states it fully. This sets up the reasoning on both sides in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot live without his head. So maybe naming the head counts as pledging his whole value. Or maybe, since the pledge is for the מזבח, he owes only the value of the head.

keyTerms.meaning: Returning to the earlier matter itself
Judged by its importance: a vital part counts as the whole
What is the law?

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rabba asked:
'The value of my head for the altar' — what is the law?
Is it judged by its importance,
phrases.notes: He means that since nobody lives without a head, it would count as his whole value.

phrases.english: or is it not judged by its importance?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the question quoted in Step 11 and looks at it directly.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does pledging the value of a vital part for the מזבח obligate the whole value, or only the part's value?

steps.title: The two sides of רבה's question
steps.stepSummary: The pull toward the whole value: in pledges of value, we never find a vital part judged as less than the whole. The pull toward the part only: for the מזבח, we never find a vital part spreading to the whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have not found in pledges of value a case that is not judged by its importance. Or perhaps: we have not found for the altar a case that is judged by its importance?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבה was unsure. It shows that two different rules pull in opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a pledge of value, and there naming a vital part normally means the whole value. But the pledge is for the מזבח, and there we do not find one limb's value spreading to the whole. The question is which rule controls.

keyTerms.meaning: We have not found
Value; pledges to give something's worth
Or perhaps

phrases.english: We have not found in pledges of value
a case that is not judged by its importance,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: or perhaps we have not found regarding the altar
a case that is judged by its importance?

steps.triggerLanguage: לא אשכחן בדמים דאינו נידון בכבודו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the question asked in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which rule decides: the rule for pledges of value, or the rule for the מזבח?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו. רבה's question is left without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבה's question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side wins, so the doubt stays open here. Earlier, רבא claimed that the ברייתא settles this kind of case, but רבה's own question, as it stands, ends without a ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's question about ״דמי ראשי לגבי מזבח״ ends as תיקו. The tension between the rule for pledges of value and the rule for the מזבח is left open.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question set out in Steps 13 and 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question of whether a vital part pledged for the מזבח counts as the whole value stays unresolved.

steps.title: Does a poor person pay less when he pledges his valuation for the altar?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about someone who says 'my ערך is upon me for the מזבח.' Does the השג יד rule, where a poor person pays only what he can afford, still apply?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If someone says, 'I take upon myself my valuation, for the altar,' what is the law? Do we judge him by what he can afford, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. A person pledged his ערך, but aimed it at the מזבח, and רבא asks whether the usual discount for a poor person still works here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a pledge of ערך goes to בדק הבית, and a poor person pays only what he can afford (השג יד). Here the pledge is marked for the מזבח, so רבא is unsure whether the poor-person discount still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question, raised a doubt that needs solving
'My valuation is upon me': a pledge to give the fixed Torah amount for one's age and gender
For the altar, meaning the money is for buying קרבנות, not for Temple upkeep
What a person can afford; a poor person pays a reduced ערך based on his means

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If someone says, 'My valuation is upon me, for the altar,' what is the law?
Is he judged by what he can afford,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:8. A poor person who can't pay the full ערך pays according to his means.

phrases.english: or is he not judged by what he can afford?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה's question about 'the value of my head for the מזבח' ended in תיקו, רבא asks a similar 'for the מזבח' question about השג יד.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the השג יד discount applies to a ערך pledged for the מזבח.

steps.title: The two sides: valuation rules versus altar rules
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out why each answer makes sense. Every ערך we know of follows השג יד, but everything for the מזבח is redeemed at its real value.
steps.simpleTranslation: On one side, we never find a valuation that is not judged by what the person can afford. On the other side, maybe we say that we never find something for the altar that is redeemed for anything except its real value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two sides of רבא's question. This sets up the תיקו that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: every ערך in the Torah follows השג יד, so this one should too. Side two: anything for the מזבח is redeemed only at its full real value, with no discounts. Two rules apply here and they pull in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: We have not found, meaning there is no known case of this
Or perhaps; brings in the other side of a doubt
Is redeemed, bought back from holiness with money
At its real value, its full market worth

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is proving anything here. Each 'we have not found' is only a reason for one side of the doubt. Neither side wins.

phrases.english: We have not found, in valuations,
a case that is not judged by what he can afford,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: or perhaps we have not found, for the altar,
anything that is redeemed except at its real value?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן בַּעֲרָכִין דְּאֵין נִידּוֹן בְּהֶשֵּׂג יָד, אוֹ דִלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind both sides of רבא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which rule wins: the ערכין rule of השג יד, or the מזבח rule of full value.

steps.title: רבא's question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבא's question with תיקו. No answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבא's question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rules carry real weight, and no source settles which one controls. So the question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it stand': the question stays unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question opened in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether השג יד applies to a ערך pledged for the מזבח is left undecided.

steps.title: An ancestral field given to the altar: fixed price or real value?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks about someone who makes a שדה אחוזה holy for the מזבח. Is it redeemed at the Torah's fixed rate of fifty shekels per חומר of barley-seed land, or at its real value?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If someone consecrated his ancestral field for the altar, what is the law? Do we say that we never find an ancestral field redeemed except at 'a חומר of barley seed for fifty silver shekels'? Or perhaps we never find something for the altar that is redeemed except at its real value?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a question with the same pattern as רבא's, this time about a family field given for the מזבח. The גמרא gives both sides right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inherited field that is made holy is normally redeemed at a fixed Torah price, based on how much seed the land takes, not on what it is really worth. But things for the מזבח are always redeemed at real value. Once again two rules clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Made something holy, giving it to the Temple
An ancestral field, land inherited in the family
Do we say...? Brings in the first side of a doubt
Land big enough to sow a חומר of barley; the unit used to set the fixed price

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same kind of question as רבא's: does a special Torah price rule still hold when the item is directed to the מזבח?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If someone consecrated an ancestral field
for the altar, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן: לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה
phrases.english: Do we say: we have not found an ancestral field
that is redeemed except
'an area for sowing a chomer of barley'
'for fifty silver shekels,'

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: or perhaps we have not found, for the altar,
anything that is redeemed except at its real value?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question built on the same 'for the מזבח, only at real value' side used in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a שדה אחוזה given for the מזבח is redeemed at the fixed Torah rate or at its real value.

steps.title: רב אשי's question also stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: Like רבא's question, רב אשי's question ends in תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves רב אשי's question open, which ends this run of 'for the מזבח' questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the fixed-price rule and the real-value rule each have strong support, and nothing decides between them.
steps.whatToRemember: All three 'for the מזבח' questions (רבה, רבא, רב אשי) end in תיקו. Each time, a special rule for vows of value clashes with the way things work for the מזבח.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב אשי's question from step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: How a שדה אחוזה given for the מזבח is redeemed is left undecided.

steps.title: A baby under one month: can be pledged by value, but has no valuation
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a baby less than a month old can be the subject of a pledge of value (נידר), but not of a ערך (נערך).
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A baby less than one month old can be pledged by his value, but he cannot be valuated.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It explains what kind of pledge works for a baby under one month old.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pledge of 'his value' (נדר) means paying what the person would sell for, and even a tiny baby has some value. The Torah's fixed ערך amounts start only from one month old, so a ערך pledge on a younger baby does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Less than one month old
Can be pledged by his market value (a נדר of דמים)
Can be valuated, meaning given a fixed Torah ערך

steps.confusionAlert: נידר and נערך sound alike but are different pledges. נידר is about real market worth. נערך is the Torah's fixed price chart, which starts at one month.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A baby less than one month old can be pledged by his value,
phrases.notes: If someone says 'this baby's worth is upon me,' he pays what the baby would sell for.

phrases.english: but he cannot be valuated.
phrases.notes: The Torah's fixed ערך amounts begin only at one month old.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ פָּחוֹת מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ נִידָּר, אֲבָל לֹא נֶעֱרָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new subject after the earlier questions closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby under one month can be the subject of a pledge of value (נידר), but not of a ערך pledge (נערך).

steps.title: A ברייתא: ערך vow on a baby under one month
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת. If someone makes a ערך vow on a baby less than a month old, רבי מאיר says he pays the baby's value. חכמים say his words mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Sages taught: If someone makes a ערך vow on a baby less than a month old, רבי מאיר says he gives the baby's value, and חכמים say he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by quoting a ברייתא. In it, רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about a ערך vow on a baby who is too young for ערך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives no ערך for a baby under a month, so the vow cannot work as a ערך. רבי מאיר says it still obligates the person to pay the baby's market value. חכמים say the vow simply does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes a ערך vow (pledges the fixed תורה amount for a person)
He gives his value (the market value, as if sold as a slave)
He said nothing; his words have no effect

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר does not say the ערך works here. He agrees there is no ערך for this baby. He only says the person owes the baby's market value (דמים) instead.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
One who makes a valuation vow on a baby less than a month old,
Rabbi Meir says: he gives the baby's value,
phrases.notes: "Value" here means what the baby would be worth on the market, not the fixed תורה amount.

phrases.english: and the Sages say: he has said nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּעֲרִיךְ פָּחוֹת מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה's rule that a baby under a month cannot have a ערך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a ערך vow on a baby under a month: רבי מאיר says he pays the baby's value; חכמים say he owes nothing.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies underneath the argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what basic principle causes רבי מאיר and חכמים to rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides know there is no ערך for a baby under a month. So the argument must come from a different question. The גמרא wants to name that question.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asking for the root idea behind a מחלוקת)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that splits רבי מאיר and חכמים.

steps.title: Does a person ever speak for no reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that a person does not say words for nothing. He knew there is no ערך for such a baby, so he must have meant its value. The רבנן hold that a person can say words for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: a person does not say his words for nothing. He knows there is no ערך for a baby under a month, so he decided to mean the baby's value. The רבנן hold: a person can say his words for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The argument is about whether we assume a person's words always mean something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads the vow so that it has some meaning. Since a ערך is impossible, the person must have meant דמים, the baby's value. The רבנן take the words as they are: he said ערך, a ערך doesn't work here, so nothing happens.

keyTerms.meaning: A person does not say his words for nothing
He made up his mind and said (he really meant it)
Meaning the value (market price), not the ערך

steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'אין אדם מוציא דבריו לבטלה' comes up in many places in ש״ס. Here it shows up as the basis of רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
a person does not say his words for nothing,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאֵין עֲרָכִין לְפָחוֹת מִבֶּן חֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: he knows there are no valuations for a baby under a month,
so he decided and spoke meaning the value;
and the Rabbis hold:
a person does say his words for nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר: אֵין אָדָם מוֹצִיא דְּבָרָיו לְבַטָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the argument depends on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר: people don't speak for nothing, so the vow means דמים. רבנן: people can speak for nothing, so the vow is empty.

steps.title: Whose view is רב's ruling about a utensil?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side agrees with רב's ruling. רב said that someone who vows the ערך of a utensil must pay its value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? רב גידל said in the name of רב: one who says 'I take upon myself the ערך of a utensil' gives its value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of רב and asks which side of the מחלוקת it matches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A utensil can never have a ערך, since ערך is only for people. Even so, רב says the person pays the utensil's value. So the גמרא wants to know which view of the ברייתא this fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
"The ערך of a utensil is upon me": a vow using ערך language for an object
He gives the value (what the item is worth)

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow,
that which Rav Giddel said in the name of Rav:
one who says, "The valuation of a utensil is upon me"
gives its value?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the principle from Step 24 to place רב's ruling on one side of the מחלוקת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side, רבי מאיר or the רבנן, agrees with רב's utensil ruling.

steps.title: It follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רב's ruling follows רבי מאיר, who holds that a person does not speak for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's ruling matches רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A utensil has no ערך, just like a baby under a month. Making the person pay its value means reading his words so they have meaning. That is רבי מאיר's principle.

phrases.english: It follows Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25's question.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: of course רב follows רבי מאיר. Why did it need to be said?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that it follows רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. It seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A utensil case looks exactly like the baby case: a ערך vow on something that has no ערך. So linking רב to רבי מאיר seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (an objection that something didn't need to be said)

phrases.english: It is obvious that it follows Rabbi Meir!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether Step 26's answer was needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that רב's ruling follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases are a ערך vow on something with no ערך, so the link is obvious and needs no mention.

steps.title: You might have thought even the רבנן agree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why it was needed. One might have said that even the רבנן agree about a utensil. With the baby, the person made an honest mistake: he thought that just as a one-month-old has a ערך, so does a younger baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that it follows even the רבנן. It is only there, with the baby, that the person makes a mistake. He thinks that just as a one-month-old baby has a ערך, a younger baby has one too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' objection. It shows a reason someone could have thought רב fits even the רבנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The baby case could be a real mistake: the person thought his words worked as a ערך, so the רבנן let him off. With a utensil, no one would think it has a ערך, so this mistake doesn't apply. That is why the גמרא needed to tell us which view רב follows.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken first thought)
He makes a mistake

steps.confusionAlert: This line only gives the 'you might have thought' (הוה אמינא). It is not the final ruling. The גמרא is explaining why the link to רבי מאיר had to be spelled out.

phrases.english: You might have said it follows even the Rabbis,
since it is only there that he makes a mistake, thinking:
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the baby under a month old.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּאִיכָּא עֲרָכִין לְבֶן חוֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: just as there are valuations for a one-month-old,
there are also valuations for one less than a month old.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' objection of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a reasonable mistaken thought that the statement comes to rule out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even the רבנן might agree in the utensil case. Their reason for letting him off with the baby is that he made an honest mistake, and no such mistake is possible with a utensil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גמרא states clearly that רב's ruling follows רבי מאיר, to block the idea that the רבנן would agree.

steps.title: A utensil leaves no room for a mistake, so the גמרא had to say רב follows only רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. With a utensil there is no room for an honest mistake, so we might have thought even the רבנן agree the person meant its value. That is why the גמרא had to teach that רב's ruling follows only רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, with a utensil, there is no way to make a mistake. A person surely knows a utensil has no ערך. So he must have meant its value when he spoke. That is what we might have thought. So the גמרא teaches us that it is not so: רב's ruling follows only רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the answer from the last step. It explains what we might have wrongly thought about a utensil, and says its own statement 'כרבי מאיר' comes to correct that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a baby under one month, the person had a reason to be confused, so the רבנן say his words had no effect. With a utensil, nobody could think it has a ערך, so we might have said everyone agrees he meant its value. The גמרא's statement 'כרבי מאיר' shows that the utensil case also depends on רבי מאיר's idea that a person does not speak for nothing. The רבנן disagree even here.

keyTerms.meaning: to make a mistake, to err
he made up his mind and said it, meaning he spoke on purpose
for the sake of its value, as a vow to give its worth in money
it teaches us, the point of the statement is to tell us something we might not have known

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling, that someone who vows the ערך of a utensil pays its value, follows only רבי מאיר. The רבנן say that even with a utensil, a person can say words for nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: The words 'a person certainly knows... he meant its value' are not the final ruling. They are what we might have thought, and the closing words 'it teaches us' reject that idea.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the real difference between רבי מאיר and the רבנן. For the רבנן, it does not matter whether the person was confused or not. Words that make no sense as said simply have no effect.

phrases.english: But here, where there is no room to make a mistake,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means רב's case of a utensil, compared with the baby under one month from the last step.

phrases.english: a person certainly knows
that there is no ערך for a utensil,
so he decided and said it for the sake of its value,
therefore it teaches us.
phrases.notes: By saying 'it follows רבי מאיר', the גמרא is teaching that the רבנן would not agree even about a utensil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the תירוץ begun in step 28. It contrasts the baby case, where a mistake was possible, with the utensil case, where it was not.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a חידוש: the statement is needed to correct something we might have wrongly thought (הוה אמינא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since nobody could think a utensil has a ערך, even the רבנן would agree that the person meant its value.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גמרא's statement 'כרבי מאיר' teaches that רב's ruling follows only רבי מאיר. The רבנן hold that a person can speak for nothing even about a utensil.
